annotation.method: Codex freshly read the complete 25-page PDF in physical order, including the MIMS cover, Sections 1-7, Theorem 2.1, Lemmas 4.1-4.2, both algorithms, both code fragments, all ten experiments, the discussion, and references, then compared every source-proved candidate with Mathlib and the frozen importable NumStability baseline.
annotation.reason: The project owner assigned the P41 source selection and benchmark annotation to Codex.

corpus_membership: This paper is part of the current corpus listed in metadata/manifest.json.
paper_version: published journal version; SIAM Journal on Scientific Computing 33(2), 2011, printed pages 488-511

rejected_candidates.candidate: The truncation and backward-error parameter analysis in Section 3
rejected_candidates.reason: The key truncation bound and parameter selection are explicitly imported from the authors' earlier scaling-and-squaring analysis rather than proved in this paper.

rejected_candidates.candidate: Lemma 4.1 as a T1 or T2 task
rejected_candidates.reason: Its hard rounded Taylor-action estimate is delegated to standard matrix-product error analysis in reference [10], while its exponential backward-error input comes from the earlier Section 3 analysis. The compiled library contains lower-level matrix-product and summation bounds but no full Taylor-action result. Isolating one or two of those lower-level cited ingredients would assume away the source lemma's main content and create an artificial task.

rejected_candidates.candidate: Lemma 4.2, first-order perturbation bound and factor-two attainability
rejected_candidates.reason: The result is source-proved and has no compiled NumStability match, but it assumes the Frechet derivative representation and vectorization identities from reference [12]. Theorem 2.1 supplies a cleaner, fully developed, and at least equally substantial self-contained T3 target.
The matrix-exponential condition-number bounds and normal-matrix equality cases used there are explicitly cited from reference [12] and Van Loan.

rejected_candidates.candidate: Algorithms 3.2 and 5.2, Code Fragments 3.1 and 5.1, and Section 6
rejected_candidates.reason: These portions specify algorithms, implementation choices, cost observations, and empirical experiments rather than additional source-proved universal results suitable for a task.

T1.decision: Skipped. No complete source-proved result needs exactly one substantial compiled NumStability theorem. Lemma 4.1 has no compiled Taylor-action theorem, and reducing it to the available one-product bound would select an externally cited lower-level fragment rather than the paper's result.

T2.decision: Skipped. No complete source-proved result receives two distinct substantial compiled-library shortcuts. Matrix multiplication and recursive summation are only lower-level ingredients of the externally delegated rounding argument in Lemma 4.1; packaging that decomposition would be artificial and would not prove the complete source lemma.

T3.decision: Selected the full arbitrary-ell and arbitrary-p column identity of Theorem 2.1, equation (2.7). Its complete block-power, shift-column, convergent-series, and reindexing proof is supplied in the paper, is substantial, and has no corresponding NumStability shortcut.

selection_policy: Use only conclusions whose statements and supporting proofs appear in this paper.
Do not turn cited truncation, matrix-product rounding, Frechet representation, or condition-number theorems into P41 tasks.
Do not weaken Theorem 2.1 to only the exponential case ell=0 or to a fixed number of columns.
Do not isolate lower-level NumStability matrix-product or summation results from Lemma 4.1 while assuming away the complete Taylor-action analysis.
Do not count generic block-matrix, finite-sum, or analytic-series infrastructure as a substantial NumStability advantage.
Assign a tier only after exact private N and L proofs compile.
